RADIOLOGY REPORT Harlan County General Hospital - Department of Radiology Patient: CHANCE, SILAS H DOB 02/19/1995 Exam date: 05/24/2089 EXAMINATION: Chest radiograph, two views, and lumbar spine radiograph. CLINICAL INDICATION: 94 year old man with dementia, found confused, possible fall, chronic back pain. COMPARISON: None in our system.
FINDINGS: Chest: Heart size is at the upper limit of normal. Mild pulmonary vascular prominence consistent with volume overload in a patient with chronic kidney disease. No focal consolidation, effusion or pneumothorax. There is a healed deformity of the left clavicle in keeping with an old fracture. A metallic chain with a small flat identification tag lies over the upper chest, outside the patient. The legible stamped lettering on the tag reads "CHANCE SILAS H US 55 417 308 T89 PROT" and, on the back, "LUCKY". This is a personal item and has been noted for the nurse. Lumbar spine: Mild multilevel degenerative disc space narrowing and anterior osteophytes. Vertebral body heights preserved. No acute fracture.
IMPRESSION: 1. Mild pulmonary vascular congestion, no pneumonia. 2. Old left clavicle fracture, healed. 3. No acute lumbar fracture; degenerative changes. 4. Identification tag over the chest, outside the body - recommend return to the patient or niece.
Dictated by Imogen Pettibone, MD, Radiology. Dictated but not read. 05/24/2089 16:41.
